title: Nonforfeiture Computation Sheet: Reduced Paid-Up Face at an Owner's Election on Whole Life Insurance
content:
Reduced paid-up insurance elected by the owner of a premium-paying Ashgrove Whole Life Insurance policy is bought by the policy's net cash value.

## Formal statement

The reduced paid-up face is the net cash value divided by the net single premium per 1,000 of paid-up insurance and multiplied by 1,000, rounded half up to the whole dollar. The net cash value is the guaranteed cash value and the paid-up additions cash value from the most recent anniversary statement, plus the dividend accumulations withdrawn for the election, less the loan principal and the loan interest extinguished at the election. The election takes effect on the paid-to date, and the reduced paid-up face must be at least the tier's smallest reduced paid-up face.

## Inputs and records

| Input | Record |
|---|---|
| Guaranteed cash value; paid-up additions cash value | The policy record, as of the most recent anniversary |
| Net single premium per 1,000 of paid-up insurance | The policy record, as of the most recent anniversary |
| Dividend accumulations withdrawn for the election | The accumulation withdrawal entry for the election on the activity history |
| Loan principal and loan interest extinguished | The principal and interest on the loan offset entry for the election (offset on the nonforfeiture occasion) |
| Effective date | The paid-to date on the policy record |

## Worked computation (hypothetical)

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Guaranteed cash value | 30000.00 |
| Paid-up additions cash value | 4000.00 |
| Accumulations withdrawn for the election | 5151.23 |
| Less loan principal extinguished | 9000.00 |
| Less loan interest extinguished | 182.50 |
| Net cash value | 29968.73 |
| Net single premium per 1,000 | 520.40 |
| 29968.73 divided by 520.40, times 1,000 | 57587.87 |
| Reduced paid-up face, rounded half up to the dollar | 57588 |

A face of 57588 dollars is above a smallest reduced paid-up face of 1000 dollars.
